cohort: 6127 mothers whose last child was <=23-month-old from the 2017 Indonesia Demographic and Health Survey.
finding: Prelacteal feeding was prevalent in Indonesia, with formula being the most frequent type, and factors associated with higher prevalence included higher wealth quintiles in rural areas, baby perceived to be small at birth, caesarean deliveries, and not having immediate skin-to-skin contact after birth.
mod_finding: Caesarean deliveries were associated with a higher prevalence of prelacteal feeding.
